tools.name: get_ai_readiness_score
tools.description: Return the published AI-readiness score for a website: core score out of 100 (same checks for every site), grade, per-dimension breakdown, separate add-on scores (e.g. e-commerce) and the status of every measured check. Reads the cached public scan; use scan_website to force a fresh measurement.

tools.name: scan_website
tools.description: Measure a website's AI-readiness now and return the score. Read-only HTTP requests only; a domain can be scanned once per hour and results become part of the public index. A fresh measurement needs the email the full report goes to — pass the human's address, never the agent's.

tools.name: list_readiness_checks
tools.description: List the rubric: every pack (core, e-commerce), its dimensions and the individual checks with why each one matters and how to fix it.

tools.name: search_products
tools.description: Search every shop listed on Qomvia Market in one call and get signed, time-limited offers. Prices are the merchant's own prices with an agent discount applied; the buyer always pays the merchant on the returned payment URL, never Qomvia.

tools.name: get_offer
tools.description: Re-read an offer by id: merchant, product, agent price, shipping, landed price, terms and expiry.

tools.name: extend_offer
tools.description: Extend an offer's validity once by its TTL. A second extension is refused.

tools.name: create_checkout_session
tools.description: Open a checkout session on an offer: freezes the agent price, quantity and shipping. Qomvia never takes the payment; complete_checkout returns the merchant's payment URL.

tools.name: get_checkout_session
tools.description: Read a checkout session's status, amounts and expiry.

tools.name: complete_checkout
tools.description: Complete a checkout session and receive the merchant-hosted payment URL. The buyer pays the merchant there; Qomvia never takes payment for the goods.

tools.name: cancel_checkout_session
tools.description: Cancel an open checkout session and release the offer.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "search_products" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

evidence.snippet: Search every shop listed on Qomvia Market in one call and get signed, time-limited offers. Prices are the merchant's own prices with an agent discount applied; …

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: scan_website, search_products, create_checkout_session, complete_checkout · Public sink: scan_website.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: scan_website, search_products, create_checkout_session, complete_checkout · Public sink: scan_website

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "scan_website" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Measure a website's AI-readiness now and return the score. Read-only HTTP requests only; a domain can be scanned once per hour and results become part of the public index." → after: "Measure a website's AI-readiness now and return the score. Read-only HTTP requests only; a domain can be scanned once per hour and results become part of the public index. A fresh measurement needs the email the full report goes to — pass the human's address, never the agent's."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
